content.value_statement: Teams often lose time keeping documentation consistent across code, APIs, architecture, and release notes. This skill provides a phased workflow that routes documentation tasks to focused helper skills.
actual_capabilities: Plans documentation structure and style guidelines.
Guides API documentation and OpenAPI specification creation.
Coordinates C4 and Mermaid architecture documentation tasks.
Supports README, tutorial, wiki, and onboarding document creation.
Routes changelog and release note work to dedicated helper skills.
Defines quality gates for keeping documentation current.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automation code.
Depends on referenced helper skills being installed and trustworthy.
Does not validate links, examples, or API schemas by itself.
Requires project context before producing accurate documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Documentation System
use_cases.description: Create a structure for project docs, style rules, ownership, and publishing steps before writing content.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Reference Material
use_cases.description: Coordinate endpoint documentation, OpenAPI specifications, examples, and authentication guides for a service.

use_cases.title: Maintain Wikis and Onboarding Docs
use_cases.description: Organize wiki pages, onboarding guides, release notes, and maintenance checks for a growing team.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Documentation Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the documentation workflow to design a documentation structure for this project: [project context]. Include audiences, priorities, and owners.

prompt_templates.title: Create README and Setup Guides
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to create a README and getting started guide for [project]. Include installation, usage, and troubleshooting sections.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate API and Architecture Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to coordinate API reference, OpenAPI specs, C4 diagrams, and Mermaid diagrams for [system]. List the required source inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Maintenance Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to audit existing documentation for [project]. Create a phased update plan covering stale content, links, examples, and release notes.

output_examples.input: Document a new REST API service.
output: A documentation plan for endpoint reference, authentication, request examples, and error handling.
A list of source inputs needed from engineering and product teams.
A publishing checklist for review, examples, and version updates.

output_examples.input: Improve an outdated README and team wiki.
output: A gap list covering setup steps, usage guidance, onboarding pages, and troubleshooting content.
A prioritized update plan with owners and review points.
Quality gates for links, examples, diagrams, and release notes.

output_examples.input: Create architecture documentation for a platform migration.
output: A proposed set of C4 diagrams, data flow notes, and deployment documentation.
A sequence for drafting, technical review, and publication.
A maintenance checklist for future architecture changes.

best_practices: Provide current project context, audience, and documentation goals before using the workflow.
Review generated content against source code, API behavior, and release history.
Treat referenced helper skills as dependencies and verify them before use.
anti_patterns: Generating documentation without checking the current implementation.
Publishing diagrams or setup steps without a human review.
Invoking unrelated helper skills when a smaller documentation task is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill help document?
faq.answer: It covers API docs, architecture docs, README files, code comments, wikis, changelogs, and onboarding guides.

faq.question: Does it generate documentation automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a workflow and prompt routing. Actual generation depends on the assistant and any referenced helper skills.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run commands or modify files by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill file contains Markdown guidance and prompt examples, not executable scripts.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the project purpose, audience, source files, API details, release history, and target documentation format.

faq.question: How should teams review the output?
faq.answer: Teams should verify facts against source code, test setup steps, check links, and review diagrams with engineers.
